environment.source: Win32_ComputerSystem, Win32_OperatingSystem, Win32_Processor and Win32_VideoController CIM instances

officialRival.verification: Downloaded archive matched adjacent official .7z.sha256. System VLC installation was not replaced.

resourceProtocol: Fresh full portable runtime/profile per run; HubThenOpen after 3s hub wait; one warmup and three measured rounds per variant with rotating launch order; default player output settings; actual 1280x720 canvas and matching DPI; media segment 20–50s; seven uniformly spaced snapshots over 30s endpoint CPU windows. Both owned players temporarily topmost at (40,40), with sampled owned-canvas, foreign-window and cursor guards before and after every snapshot. No competing task builds/tests/profilers during this batch. All 12 runs passed. Full runtime manifests, launch settings and observer hashes are in raw comparison.

interpretation.supportedObservations: H264 current build has lower observed private RAM, resident working set, dedicated GPU allocation and calibrated process-cycle demand, with nonoverlapping three-run ranges. These observations do not establish identical decoder/filter/output quality or a universal player ranking.
interpretation.cpuCounters: Raw Windows sampled CPU-time/wall-time favors VLC. Raw cycles/sec favors Aperture. Separate calibrated cycle rows use five measured invariant-TSC/QPC intervals and independent thread/process busy-counter checks, validated on the exact same CPU/24 LP/Windows boot. Original CPU-time evidence is retained, never overwritten.
interpretation.storage: Complete packaged runtime footprints differ in feature inventories, plugins and languages; no feature-matched storage win is claimed.
interpretation.hiddenHubTrim: Before/current dedicated GPU allocation remains about108.57MiB. Smaller nominal hidden swapchain capacity is not evidence of reclaimed physical GPU memory.
interpretation.qualityReadiness: One controlled visible run per player matched known sentinel phase0 then phase2 after an owned seek24. Bounds include observer/control delay, so no latency ranking. Sparse pixels do not prove full image parity or presentation cadence. No resource CPU numbers are taken from the controlled seek experiment.
interpretation.remaining: Fresh post-prune H264/AV1/HEVC matrix, effective decoder/drop/cadence checks, first-visible-video readiness, broader core workflows and output-quality comparisons remain to be verified.
